items.title: LeBron and the 76ers are showing the Raptors how to use Scottie Barnes
items.content:

(Photo by Mark Blinch/Getty Images) | Getty Images	There was a big part of me that dreaded LeBron James’ return to the Eastern Conference. The years of LeBronto, and the idea of James in his twilight years snuffing out the Raptors’ playoff hopes in infancy was almost more than I could bear. 

Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, James, and Embiid. Lord have mercy. 

But then, Shams Charania made something clear: LeBron James would not just be playing power-forward for the Sixers. Rather, he’ll be slotting in at the point guard for at least a significant amount of time. This means that the 76ers’ lineup may actually be James, Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, and Embiid. This is a game changer. And not just for the 76ers, but for the Raptors as well.

Shams Charania on LeBron James’ role in Philadelphia:

“I do expect him to play a significant time as that initiator, the game manager, the point guard of this team that sets the table for Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, and VJ Edgecombe” pic.twitter.com/ZDl78YqJ4X

— NBABase (@TheNBABase) July 28, 2026People deemed successors to LeBron have frequently fallen short in some way. Paolo Banchero and Zion Williamson both haven’t quite developed into the archetype of unstoppable point forward, but I would argue that Scottie Barnes is closer to what LeBron is archetypically — a do-it-all forward who rebounds and passes as well as scores — than any of these score-first bigs that usually get compared to LeBron. 

Since the end of the regular season, I’ve been an advocate of giving Scottie Barnes official point guard status; in a short sample size at the end of the year, Barnes showed that he was more than capable of dishing out assists as needed when Immanuel Quickley was out. In his Instagram bio, Scottie still proclaims himself to be a “6’9 PG”, and I wonder why this hasn’t been made explicit yet?

As Scottie is breaking out as a developing scorer and as one of the league’s premier defenders, I feel like his ability to facilitate an offence shouldn’t be thought of as an afterthought, lumping him into the “point forward” group. LeBron James, who famously played every position at least once in his career, saw one of his highest highs playing PG for the LA Lakers in 2020, leading the league in assists with 10.2 per game, and coming second in MVP voting. That was, in my view, one of his finest seasons in a very storied career. Am I saying that slotting Scottie in at the one is going to be what finally turns him into a superstar? 

Yes. I think it just might.

items.title: Bucks Hesitant To Offer First Round Pick In Trade For Peyton Watson
items.content:
The Milwaukee Bucks are one of several teams actively engaged in sign-and-trade talks for Denver Nuggets forward Peyton Watson. One holdup on the Bucks side is that the team is reluctant to include a first-round pick in exchange for Watson.

Denver is said to be seeking a package that includes first-round picks, young talent or a combination of the two. If Milwaukee is unwilling to include draft capital, they may need to part with rotation players to acquire Watson. One player who could be of interest to the Nuggets is Jaime Jaquez, who the Bucks acquired earlier this summer in trade for Giannis Antetokounmpo.

The Atlanta Hawks, Cleveland Cavaliers and LA Clippers have also been linked to Watson. Denver re-signing Watson themselves also hasn't been ruled out.

items.title: Knicks Draftee Jack Kayil Signs With ALBA Berlin
items.content:
New York Knicks 2026 draftee Jack Kayil has signed with ALBA Berlin. Reports out of Germany are that Kayil signed a five-year contract with Berlin.

Kayil spent last season with ALBA Berlin while on loan from KK Mega Bemax in Serbia. In 65 games with Berlin, the 6-foot-3 guard averaged 12.2 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.6 assists and 1.0 steals in 21.4 minutes per game.

It's likely that Kayil's new deal has some form of NBA out over the course of the five seasons. The 20-year-old had expressed an interest in coming to the NBA as earlier as this coming season. Kayil averaged 8.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.8 steals at Summer League for the Knicks.

items.title: James Harden gun charge dismissed following June arrest
items.content:
NBA free agent James Harden will no longer face charges following a June arrest in Houston. Harden — who was charged with unlawfully carrying a weapon — had those charges dismissed Thursday after he completed an "alternative resolution agreement," per multiple reports. 

Harden, 36, was arrested in June after a traffic stop. During that stop, officers noticed Harden had a handgun in plain view and unholstered. That led to his arrest and charge. 

Harden was held on $100 bond and released later the same day.

At the time, the Cleveland Cavaliers — Harden's most-recent NBA team — released a statement confirming they were aware of the situation, but would not comment further. Though Harden is still a free agent, it's believed he will eventually sign a new, multi-year contract to return to the Cavaliers. 

Unlawfully carrying a weapon is a misdemeanor in Texas. Because of that, it wasn't certain that he would face punishment from the NBA following his arrest. 

With the charge now dropped, it seems less likely the NBA will get involved. That should pave the way for Harden to pick his next team and have an uninterrupted regular season. 

Despite his age, Harden remains an effective scorer. After a midseason trade from the Los Angeles Clippers to the Cavaliers, Harden averaged 20.5 points in 26 games with Cleveland.

items.title: Clippers, Jamarion Sharp Finalize Two-Way Deal
items.content:
August 7: The Clippers have officially signed Sharp to a two-way contract, per NBA.com’s transaction log.

L.A. also reportedly intends to waive Pedulla and sign guard Jalen Pickett to a two-way deal.

July 21: The Clippers and free agent center Jamarion Sharp have agreed to terms on a two-way contract, agent Scott Nichols tells Michael Scotto of HoopsHype (Twitter link).

Sharp, who will turn 25 in August, went undrafted out of Ole Miss in 2024 and has played primarily for the Texas Legends in the G League since then. The 7’5″ big man had a huge year for the Legends in 2025/26, earning a spot on the G League’s All-Defensive team and being named NBAGL Defensive Player of the Year after leading the league with 3.9 blocks per game.

Sharp’s rim protection is his calling card. He also led the NCAA in blocked shots in 2021/22 (4.6 per game) and 2022/23 (4.1) while playing for Western Kentucky. Playing for the Raptors at the Las Vegas Summer League this month, he averaged 7.4 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 2.8 blocks in just 18.2 minutes per game across five appearances.

As Scotto notes, the expectation is that Sharp will provide depth in the middle for the Clippers while Yanic Konan Niederhauser recovers following a pair of procedures on his right foot. While the team hasn’t shared a recovery timeline for Niederhauser, it would be a surprise if he’s ready for opening night.

Sean Pedulla and 2026 second-round pick Nick Martinelli currently hold two-way contracts for the Clippers, leaving one open slot, so no corresponding roster move will be necessary to officially sign Sharp.
